reasons: The AUDIT rule constrains a Vendor-favourable right; the cited paragraphs contain no audit, inspection, verification or system-access right running against the Customer (Sparkling), so the outcome is at or better than the preferred position.

Cited text supports the rationale: § 3 (p0029-p0035) imposes only substantive use restrictions with no verification or reporting mechanic; the 'accounting records for which access is obtained' language in p0095 is definitional scoping inside a mutual confidentiality clause, not a grant of access; the only examination right (p0114, escrow materials) runs in the Customer's favour.

Consistent with a compliant claim, no redline was rendered and no comment proposed — appropriate here, since raising the point would invite the Vendor to introduce a verification right the Customer does not currently owe.

The failed deterministic check ('audit frequency limited') is a heuristic artefact of the total absence of an audit clause rather than evidence of an unconstrained audit right, and does not warrant a deviation or missing classification for a protective rule whose absence benefits our party.
